"We are seeing early signs of stability, both in the wider Saudi economy, where GDP recovered slightly from Q2, and in purchase order activity from our clients," said Adam Zaghloul, Vice President of Strategy & Planning at NTG Clarity. "Purchase orders were $33.4 million in the third quarter and we have announced a further $24.5 million since. Our focus now is staffing those orders and turning them into billings. Collections improved in the quarter, bringing receivables and unbilled contract assets down, and that progress has continued into the fourth quarter. We have worked with our clients on pricing and billing through a difficult period, and we believe that is how long-term relationships in the Kingdom are built."

The prolonged conflict in the Middle East has disrupted oil shipments through the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, on which many digitization initiatives in Saudi Arabia and the rest of the Gulf rely for funding. Saudi enterprises have responded with a focus on cost savings and return on investment. Some customers have negotiated more favourable pricing, paused expansion and in some cases scaled back their engagements.

Revenue declined again in Q3 as these adjustments took effect. However, order intake has been steadier, starting in Q3 and extending into the fourth quarter, with an increased pace of new purchase orders, a four-year extension of an existing framework agreement and a new three-year framework agreement with a new customer. NTG has worked with its customers through this period on pricing, on billing terms and on the size of their engagements. The Company believes that supporting its customers during these difficult conditions strengthens its standing in the region. The new framework agreement announced on November 17, 2026 marks the fourth portfolio company of one of the Kingdom's largest investment entities to become an NTG customer and is a sign of the growing position of NTG within some of the most prestigious companies in the region.

Management is continually evaluating the prospects for future growth against its delivery capacity with an eye towards cash generation and improving profitability. NTG's top priority is cash collections and receivables management so that it remains self-funded during the turbulence in the Middle East. Q3 showed progress, with an overall reduction in accounts receivable due to strong collections and no bad debts expected. Those collections continued into Q4, which showed receivables decreasing by approximately a further $4M by the end of October.

NTG references Adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-IFRS (non-GAAP) measure and Adjusted EBITDA margin, which is a non-GAAP ratio. Adjusted EBITDA means adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. EBITDA is equal to net income (loss) before income taxes plus finance costs plus depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is equal to EBITDA before other discretionary expenses and expenses outside of the control of NTG. In NTG's case these are other income, share-based payments, and expenses related to foreign exchange. Adjusted EBITDA margin is Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue.

Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are not recognized measures under IFRS. Management believes that in addition to net income (loss), Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are useful supplemental measures as they provide an indication of the results generated by the Company's primary business activities prior to consideration of how those activities are financed, amortized, or how the results are taxed and consolidated in various jurisdictions and currencies as well as the cash generated by the Company's primary business activities without consideration of the timing of the monetization of non-cash working capital items.

Readers should be cautioned, however, that Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin should not be construed as an alternative to net income determined in accordance with IFRS as an indicator of the Company's performance. The Company's method of calculating Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin may differ from other organizations and, accordingly, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin may not be comparable to measures used by other organizations.
